titleEn: One More Try, and One More!

pages.text: "There's no sound!" Mumu put a shell down on the porch. Blowing into it made only a windy noise. Mumu had found the smooth shell in the stream that morning.
"I want it to go peeee!" Quick-handed monkey Taro climbed onto the porch. "I'd like to hear it!"
Mumu blew ten times. Only air sounded. "I can't do it." Mumu threw the shell away, and it rolled along the porch's edge.
Taro reached quickly and caught it. "You've only tried ten times." He set it back in front of Mumu.
"Make your mouth small, like this." Taro tapped the porch twice with a branch. Mumu's ears turned to the sound. "Blow in time with this."
Whooo—peep! A tiny sound came out. "It worked! There's a sound!" Taro clapped. "One More Try, and One More!"
The next try made only air again. But Mumu did not throw the shell. "That's okay. One More Try, and One More!"
Mumu lifted it to their mouth again. Peeeee! Peeeee! The sound reached the porch's far edge. Grandma looked up from preparing food. "Who brought a bird?"
Mumu held the shell tightly. "One, don't throw it away! Two, change something a little! Three, try once more!" Beside them, Taro nodded once.

Taro put an arm around Mumu's neck and wrapped his tail around their back. Something that failed could work one day after another try. Mumu held the shell close to their mouth. "One More Try, and One More!"
